chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who forcibly violated a woman sexually. He said: “He is to be killed, whether he is muḥṣan or not muḥṣan.”

key_terms.غَيْرَ مُحْصَنٍ: not legally married or without muḥṣan status
key_terms.فَرْجَهَا: her private part, meaning sexual violation
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally married or sexually protected status

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a man who forcibly violates a woman?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling concerning a man who forcibly violates a woman. Imām Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام rules that the perpetrator is to be killed regardless of whether he is muḥṣan or non-muḥṣan, indicating the gravity of this crime in Islamic jurisprudence.
